text.p: - MSAS Cargo International Ltd said it has setup a partnership with Toronto forwarder, Same Right-O-Way Courier Express Cargo to provide a "more focused Canadian network."
Sameday, which has 32 service centres across Canada, will represent MSAS where the latter does not have it own offices, MSAS added in a statement.
This includes Calgary, Edmonton,, Halifax, Winnipeg and support operations in MSAS offices in Fort Erie, Lacolle, Montreal, Ottawa, Toronto, Vancouver and Windsor, it said.

In Newfoundland, St John's will be added at a later date. The statement said MSAS will capitalise on Sameday's domestic feed into its gateways in Toronto, Montreal, Ottawa, Vancouver, while Sameday's international shipments will be transferred to the MSAS network.

MSAS Canada managing director, Tim Speed said this gives "our customers the confidence that we have far greater control over their shipments than when we had several agent partners across the country."
He added the move "builds on the success of the new Toronto Gateway, opened 18 months ago, which has increased its volumes to 800 tonnes from 200 tonnes over the period."
The new partnership came into effect on April 1 and replaces previous agreements with three Canadian agent partners, an MSAS spokeswoman said.
These were with Farrow International in Calgary and Edmonton, Atlantic Customers Brokers Ltd in Halifax and George H.Young & Co Ltd from Winnipeg.
MSAS forms part of the London-based Ocean Group Plc international logistics, marine and environmental services group.
